# lightningcss light-dark() downlevel: var() pairs freeze at :root, don't re-resolve per-descendant

`@pantoken/css`'s token sheets express dark mode via `light-dark()`. lightningcss downlevels this to
`--instui-color-x: var(--lightningcss-light, A) var(--lightningcss-dark, B);`, declared ONCE on
`:root`. `--lightningcss-light`/`-dark` are set via `[data-pantoken-scheme="light"|"dark"]` attribute
rules (see canvas-theme-editor's `PREVIEW_SCHEME_FORCE_CSS`).

**Gotcha:** overriding `--lightningcss-light`/`-dark` (or even the derived `--instui-color-*` token)
on a DESCENDANT element (e.g. `#some-panel { --lightningcss-dark: initial; }`) does NOT change that
descendant's inherited `--instui-color-*` value, no matter how high the specificity (inline style,
`!important`, ID selector — all fail). This is because CSS custom-property `var()` substitution
resolves at the element that DECLARES the property, not lazily at each point of inheritance/use —
`:root`'s `--instui-color-x` is already a frozen, fully-resolved color by the time it inherits down.

**To actually force a different scheme for one subtree:** re-declare the FULL token sheet a second
time scoped to that subtree's own selector (e.g. `tokensCss.replaceAll(":root", "#my-panel")`), in
the SAME injected stylesheet as (or after) a rule setting `--lightningcss-light`/`-dark` for that
same selector. Only then do the subtree's own descendants inherit a locally-recomputed value.

Diagnose this class of bug by testing with `element.style.setProperty(finalLeafVar, literalColor)`
(bypassing the whole chain) — if THAT works but overriding `--lightningcss-*` doesn't, this is the
cause. Also: `element.style.setProperty(name, "")` REMOVES the property (spec behavior) — it does
NOT set it to a genuinely empty value the way `name: ;` does in a stylesheet rule; don't use it to
simulate an empty-but-valid custom property value during debugging.

Found while debugging packages/scaffold/templates/canvas-theme-editor — ultimately not needed there
(the user clarified the tray should just inherit the interface theme like normal chrome), but the
technique is real and this note is for the next time a subtree genuinely needs a forced scheme.

## Summary

Implemented all 8 canvas-theme-editor refinements, with one correction along the way:

1. **Popup device-icon contrast** & **4. interface theme incomplete** — same root cause: `chromeThemeStyle` never got `PREVIEW_SCHEME_FORCE_CSS`, so chrome buttons/text stayed pinned to OS `prefers-color-scheme` instead of the explicit toggle. Fixed by appending it in `applyChromeTheme()`.

3. **Layout toggle disabled during popup** — wired `layoutDirectionToggle.disabled` in `openPreviewPopup`/`restorePreviewFromPopup`.
5. **Tray dark mode** — implemented then **reverted** per your clarification: the tray is regular app chrome and should follow the interface theme like everything else; only the preview `srcdoc` is independent. `applyChromeTheme()` is back to its simple form.
6. **Row-by-default** — fixed alongside the `.panes` rename; added the missing `layoutDirectionLabel` i18n key.
7. **Dock icon** — added a `prefers-color-scheme: dark`-matched icon/apple-touch-icon pair from the existing `icon-reversed.svg`.
8. **Icon-picker typeahead** — Simple Icons' SVGs lack `width`/`height` (only `viewBox`), causing oversized/blurry rendering; pinned glyph size via a `classes` hook and dropped the redundant source-label column.

All changes verified live in the browser (both guide and tool mode) and via `vp test`/`vp check` across `@pantoken/scaffold`, `@pantoken/tinymce`, and `@pantoken/docs`. Added two changesets. Saved a repo-memory note on the CSS custom-property gotcha (`var()` pairs freeze at `:root`, don't re-resolve per-descendant) that caused the tray investigation to take a wrong turn initially.
